title: allhands-field-briefing-stickerboard-sep-28-2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of highlights and sticky notes from today’s org-wide engineering all-hands. Target audience: eng-serving-runtime + platform leads who couldn’t join. This is intentionally light — think stickerboard + quick actions, not a full transcript.

Attendees (live): Maya, Liam, Aisha, Jasper, Priya, Omar, Elena, ~45 others (org attendance list in Confluence-1248).

Opening (Maya) — 5m
- One-line framing: shipping predictable SLOs for Q4; tighten canary feedback loops; reduce tail latency for 4096-token workloads.
- Shoutouts: infra team’s hotfix for nvlink flakiness (linked artifact Jira SRV-8891).

Top-level metrics snapshot (Priya) — 6m
- 99th p50/p95/p99 by model class: small (p50 12ms, p95 42ms, p99 120ms), medium (p50 28ms, p95 110ms, p99 360ms), long-context (p50 48ms, p95 210ms, p99 920ms). Note: long-context p99 spiked last night due to cache miss storm.
- Cost signal: average token cost down 6% MoM after recent batching changes, but dedicated reserved capacity customers saw two penalty billing events due to missed health-checks. Action item below.

Feature / Program updates (round-robin) — 20m
- Autoscaling policies (Liam)":
  - Canary of dynamic scale-down is live in two clusters; observed reduced over-provisioning during low-traffic windows.
  - Open risk: slow pod termination caused brief imbalance — SRE investigating SIGTERM cascade.
  - TODO: add pre-stop hook to flush KV caches before termination (owner: Jasper, due: 2026-10-05).

- Model routing and fallback (Aisha)":
  - Beta routing policy supports priority-based fallbacks across regions. Exercised successfully for a simulated eu-west outage.
  - Outstanding: document compatibility matrix for quantized variants (linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/481).
  - ACTION: product+applied-ml to finalize compatibility table (owner: Aisha, collaborator: Dan, due: 2026-10-02).

- KV/prefix cache improvements (Jasper)":
  - Rolling deploy to 30% of traffic; typical hit-rate +17% for chat workloads with short-turn exchanges.
  - Edge-case: cache invalidation race with parallel completion updates; root cause: non-atomic writes in Redis shim.
  - Quick fix: use versioned writes; medium-term: migrate hot keys to in-pod LRU (owner: Jasper, spike: this sprint).

- Observability + Console (Elena)":
  - New per-decision debug trace added to Console (opt-in) for canaries; visible in nightly canary dashboards.
  - Request: product to prioritize per-route retention for 7-day window for enterprise customers (ask sent to product-ops).

Incidents / Postmortems — 8m
- Linked incident: LATE-2026-09-26 (nvlink flake). Short postmortem in Confluence. Key takeaways: better health-check granularity and circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Billing glitches for reserved capacity: two customers billed penalty fees due to health-check flaps during maintenance window. Finance loop opened; action: add scheduled-maintenance suppression window (owner: Ops, due: 2026-10-03).

Cross-team dependencies and blocker stickers — 7m
- Private deploy packaging: Legal needs updated EULA wording before next on-prem customer pilot (owner: Legal + Product Security, blocker).
- Onboarding docs for Dedicated customers missing a step about KMS key rotation — docs patch needed (owner: Developer Experience, PR draft in repo).
- SRE needs access to a customer’s private deployment logs for debugging (request ticket created: JIRA-LOG-774).

Q&A highlights (selected) — 6m
- Q: Will we accelerate long-context optimization work? A: Yes — two spikes approved this quarter; expect micro-optimizations (kernel scheduling) followed by a single larger refactor if gains plateau.
- Q: Any change to pricing model for quantized variants? A: No immediate changes; pricing working group will present recommendations by mid-Oct.

Sticky notes / informal items (notes-to-self style) — 6m
- Reminder: bring an SLA war-room runbook to next all-hands (template exists in Confluence-ops-runbooks).
- Collect 3–5 representative long-context prompts from product teams for bench profiling (owner: Maya).
- Try small experiment: 1:1 pairing between SRE oncall + customer success for high-touch dedicated customers during first 72h of onboarding.

Action items (clear owners + due dates) — quick list:
- Pre-stop KV flush hook: Jasper — 2026-10-05
- Compatibility matrix for quantized model fallbacks: Aisha + Dan — 2026-10-02
- Add scheduled-maintenance suppression for reserved capacity billing: Ops — 2026-10-03
- Docs patch for Dedicated KMS rotation step: DevEx — 2026-10-04
- Collect long-context prompts for profiling: Maya — 2026-10-01
- SRE access request for customer private logs: (JIRA-LOG-774) — SRE lead — 2026-09-30

Open questions / parking lot (to resolve in follow-up threads)
- Should we relax p99 SLO targets for long-context models while we iterate on kernel work? (Product + Applied ML decision)
- Is there appetite for a quarterly on-call rotation swap to reduce burnout? (SRE + Eng managers)

Closing notes and tone check
- Overall mood measured: focused but tired. Many cross-team hands on micros to stabilize Q4 ramp. Keep comms short and use PR/issue links for details.
- Next all-hands: schedule poll for October window (Maya to send Doodle).

Attachments and pointers:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1248 (all-hands agenda + recording link)
- Incident postmortem: LATE-2026-09-26
- Jira: SRV-8891, JIRA-LOG-774
- GitHub: PR 481 (serving-runtime), devex docs draft branch

Appendix (raw standup blurbs captured live)
- Priya: "saw a weird spike in tail yesterday — looking into hot keys causing mem pressure"
- Liam: "scale-down looks promising but we need more graceful termination"
- Jasper: "working on Redis shim versioned writes; will drop a spike doc later today"
- Aisha: "routing fallbacks beta is ready for broader trials — need compatibility table completed"

END OF NOTES

Unresolved: leave this doc in 'in_review' until action owners confirm due dates (pinged via Slack #eng-serving-runtime).

-- Maya (notes captured live)
